messages:

Subject: Request: SLA commitments & scan evidence for SOC2/SIG

Hi Kimberly —

Following up from our vendor security intake: Acme's procurement needs a concise statement of Redwood Inference's vulnerability management commitments to satisfy our SOC2 and SIG review. Specifically we need:

- A clear SLA window for critical (CVSS 9-10), high (7-8.9), and medium (4-6.9) CVEs (time-to-remediate targets).
- Scan cadence and tooling used (internal/external scanners) and how you handle false positives.
- Evidence artifacts: most recent authenticated external scan, sample internal scan, and an attestation that you commit to SLA windows.
- Escalation/exception process for customer-impacting fixes and temporary mitigations.

Can you provide a short attestation and attach the artifacts (or a secure link)? Our audit deadline is 2027-06-10, so we need this by 2027-06-03.

Thanks —
Patricia

Subject: Re: Request: SLA commitments & scan evidence for SOC2/SIG

Patricia —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide an attestation and the requested artifacts by your deadline. Summary below; full artifacts attached.

Attached (redwood_vm_sla_attestation_20270601.pdf, scan-cadence-202705.zip) include the signed statement and the scan bundles with redaction of customer-identifying data. Key commitments:

- SLA targets (Redwood vulnerability horizon):
  * Critical (CVSS 9-10): initial triage within 4 hours, mitigation or documented compensating control within 72 hours.
  * High (7-8.9): initial triage within 24 hours, mitigation within 14 calendar days.
  * Medium (4-6.9): initial triage within 3 business days, mitigation within 45 calendar days.

- Scan cadence:
  * External authenticated scan: monthly (Nessus/Qualys) with a rotating IP set; last run included in zip (May 2027).
  * Internal authenticated scans: weekly (open-source + commercial mix) with triage tickets auto-created in Jira.
  * Continuous dependency scanning for third-party libs (SCA) with daily feeds and weekly batched alerts.

- False positives and verification: dedicated triage queue; every external finding is verified by an on-call engineer before classification. We include a sample FP reconciliation sheet in the bundle.

- Escalation and exception process:
  * Customer-impacting or exploitable-in-the-wild findings trigger our Incident Response runbook and are escalated to the on-call security lead and the product owner. Temporary mitigations (WAF rules, network ACLs) are applied within 24 hours when feasible.
  * Exceptions to SLA require an approved risk acceptance record (ticket in Jira) and a compensating control with re-review at 30/60/90 days.

Next steps: I will route the signed attestation and a sanitized scan bundle to your secure file transfer link. If you need a DocuSign for formal sign-off, I can add it.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Neha —

Couple of operational clarifications for Patricia to include in the artifact set (I added as inline so Patricia has visibility):

- Patch windows: for infra-level fixes that require rolling restarts we target a 72-hour maintenance window; we will communicate scheduled restarts and provide a post-merge verification report.

- CVE lifecycle tracking: every triaged CVE is tracked in our vulnerability tracker with fields: discovery-date, triage-owner, SLA-category, remediation-plan, mitigation-applied, and closure-verification. Sample tracker CSV is in the zip.

- Backporting policy: for models or runtime libs that affect multiple clusters we include backport timelines in the remediation plan; critical public-exploit CVEs are prioritized for immediate backports and emergency releases.

Patricia — if you need evidence of a recent critical-to-closure example, we can include a redacted timeline (ticket + commits + release notes) from March 2027 as an exemplar.

Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
